r.정치 구도: A parliamentary system in which the prime minister holds real power and the president is largely ceremonial. For decades two parties, the Awami League and the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, took turns in power, each persecuting the other in office. In 2024 student protests against quotas in civil service hiring grew into a movement to topple the government, and the prime minister of more than 15 years fled to India. The interim government banned the Awami League's activities, and in November 2025 a special tribunal sentenced the former prime minister to death in absentia over the crackdown on the protests. In the February 2026 election the Bangladesh Nationalist Party won more than two-thirds of the seats, and a referendum held the same day approved a reform charter that includes term limits for prime ministers and a new upper house. An alliance led by the Islamist party Jamaat-e-Islami became the main opposition, and when and how to carry out the charter is now the central question.

t.why: It is the world's second-largest clothing exporter after China, making garments for many of the best-known global brands. After the Rana Plaza factory building near Dhaka collapsed in 2013, killing more than 1,100 people, global brands began taking direct part in factory safety inspections. About a million Rohingya, most of whom fled persecution by Myanmar's military from 2017 onward, live in camps around Cox's Bazar in the southeast, among the largest refugee camps in the world. As a low-lying delta where great rivers meet the sea, it is hit hard by floods, cyclones and rising sea levels. It was due to graduate from the UN's list of least developed countries in November 2026, but at the new government's request the UN pushed that back three years to November 2029.
t.rel: Almost entirely surrounded by India, so rivers, borders and migration are always intertwined. It hosts around a million Rohingya refugees who fled Myanmar.
t.korea: Diplomatic relations were established in December 1973. In 1979 the Bangladeshi garment maker Desh teamed up with Korea's Daewoo and sent about 130 staff to its factory in Busan to learn the trade; most of them went on to found their own factories, helping the country's garment industry take off. In 1980 the Korean clothing company Youngone opened a factory in Chattogram, and today it runs the Korean Export Processing Zone there, Bangladesh's first private export processing zone. Samsung Electronics also has a research and development center in Dhaka. Since 2008 Bangladeshi workers have come to work in Korean factories under Korea's Employment Permit System.
t.know: Protests to defend the Bengali language in 1952 led UNESCO to make that day, February 21, International Mother Language Day.
etext: Low wages and a large workforce let it turn out T-shirts, trousers and knitwear cheaply and in bulk. Clothing makes up most of its exports, and much of the factory workforce is female.
Large numbers of its workers are employed in the Middle East, Malaysia and elsewhere, and the money they send home is a major source of foreign currency.

It makes most of the medicines it uses at home and exports a growing amount of generic drugs, helped greatly by being allowed, as a least developed country, to delay applying pharmaceutical patent rules.

Exports are concentrated in clothing, and leaving the least-developed category will cut the duty-free access it enjoys in Europe and elsewhere. Power and gas are often in short supply, and its banks carry many bad loans.
